subject: medicine
title: Multiple Sclerosis: Demyelination, Diagnostics, and Disease Modification

steps.tx: A chronic autoimmune inflammatory neurodegenerative disorder of the central nervous system characterised by recurrent episodes of inflammatory demyelination and axonal transection is **multiple sclerosis** (MS). Mediated primarily by autoreactive CD4 positive Th1 and Th17 lymphocytes targeting myelin basic protein and proteolipid protein, it predominantly affects young adults between twenty and forty years of age.
steps.say: A chronic autoimmune inflammatory neurodegenerative disorder of the central nervous system characterized by recurrent demyelination and axonal injury is multiple sclerosis. Mediated by autoreactive T lymphocytes targeting myelin proteins, it predominantly affects young adults between twenty and forty years of age.

steps.tx: The most frequent initial presentation of multiple sclerosis is acute inflammatory demyelination of the optic nerve, designated as **optic neuritis**. Patients present with acute, painful unilateral vision loss, impaired colour desaturation (dyschromatopsia), and an afferent pupillary defect, frequently exhibiting transient worsening of visual acuity and neurological symptoms during passive heating or physical exertion, termed Uhthoff phenomenon.

steps.tx: Another classic physical sign reflecting posterior column cervical cord demyelination is an electric shock-like sensation radiating down the spine into the extremities upon active neck flexion, recognized as **Lhermitte sign**. Diagnostic confirmation requires magnetic resonance imaging demonstrating dissemination in space (lesions in periventricular, juxtacortical, infratentorial, or spinal regions) and dissemination in time.
steps.say: Another classic physical sign reflecting cervical spinal cord demyelination is an electric shock-like sensation radiating down the spine upon neck flexion, recognized as Lhermitte sign. Diagnostic confirmation requires MRI demonstrating dissemination in space and time under McDonald criteria.

steps.tx: On sagittal FLAIR and T2-weighted brain magnetic resonance imaging, perivenular inflammatory demyelination produces pathognomonic ovoid hyperintense lesions oriented perpendicularly to the lateral ventricles along medullary veins, universally designated as **Dawson fingers**. Formal clinical verification of dissemination relies on the revised McDonald criteria.

steps.tx: Lumbar puncture analysis supports the diagnosis by demonstrating intrathecal immunoglobulin synthesis. Agarose gel electrophoresis with isoelectric focusing detects two or more cerebrospinal fluid-restricted **oligoclonal bands** that are completely absent in matched serum samples, indicating compartmentalized B-cell clonal expansion within the central nervous system.

steps.tx: Acute relapses of multiple sclerosis are managed with high-dose intravenous methylprednisolone (one gram daily for three to five days) to accelerate functional recovery. Long-term disease-modifying therapies (DMTs) reduce relapse rates and delay disability progression, utilizing injectable interferon beta, oral fingolimod, or high-efficacy monoclonal antibodies such as the alpha-4 integrin blocker **natalizumab**.

Long-term disease-modifying therapies reduce relapse rates and disability progression, utilizing injectable interferon beta, oral sphingosine-1-phosphate modulators, or monoclonal antibodies like natalizumab.

steps.tx: A distinct autoimmune astrocytopathy frequently misdiagnosed as multiple sclerosis is **neuromyelitis optica** (NMO, Devic disease). Clinically characterised by severe bilateral sequential optic neuritis and longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (LETM spanning three or more contiguous vertebral segments), the pathognomonic diagnostic biomarker is circulating IgG autoantibodies directed against aquaporin-4 water channels.

steps.tx: Another primary demyelinating syndrome targeting myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein is **MOG antibody disease**, presenting with recurrent bilateral optic neuritis and conus medullaris myelitis. In children following a viral prodrome, acute monophasic widespread demyelination involving both white matter and deep grey nuclei defines acute disseminated encephalomyelitis (ADEM), responding robustly to high-dose corticosteroids.
